Among all three-grade reports stating 48 pairs for these twelve schools, the tertiles expect the fewest wrong directions.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **At the tertiles’ disclosure.** Across 34,650 reports at N = 48, tertiles win with E = 1.83 (next 1.91).
- **Between feasible disclosures.** At N = 46, the lower hull reaches .455 with mixture weight .500.
- **A lower mixture.** At N = 30, the hull reaches .00517 with mixture weight .167.
- **Other cuts, full range.** Cuts 1 and 2 state 21 pairs with E = 1.12 across the full range.

<details>
<summary>Randomization and scope notes</summary>

Only three groups of four can reach 48 stated pairs. A randomized rule averaging 48 pairs must put weight exclusively on maximum-disclosure reports, so randomization cannot improve on the tertiles at 48. At intermediate disclosures, the mixture weight is the probability of choosing the report that states more pairs, while Data provides the complete error histogram and the five least-error grade vectors at N = 48. This twelve-school teaching subset is conditional on a statewide prior fitted to 5,834 eligible schools (prior-estimation uncertainty is not propagated). California's Dashboard colors follow separate rules, and this distribution provides no measure of school quality, causal effects, or statewide calibration. Related: [Reasons for a withheld comparison](../criteria/why-withheld.qmd) · [The error–disclosure frontier](../grades/frontier.qmd).

</details>

Data: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26, adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (`pr_case_cde`); <https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp>; not relicensed, provided as is; No CDE endorsement is implied.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## In postrank

This call uses the supplied posterior to evaluate the fixed tertiles at τ .20.

```r
library(postrank)
g <- pr_case_cde$reference$actions$observed_rate_tertiles
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_case_cde$input, weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = .2)[c("N", "E", "primary_risk")]
```
:::
